angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 126,617 km at 26.65 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 37.5225 +/- 0.0392 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12): 26.65 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.182 +/- 0.007 solar radii from Peterson et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LP 791-18 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023Natur.617..701P/abstract): 126,617 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.139 +/- 0.005 solar masses from Peterson et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LP 791-18 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023Natur.617..701P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 2960 +/- 55 K from Peterson et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LP 791-18 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023Natur.617..701P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Peterson et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LP 791-18 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023Natur.617..701P/abstract)

luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LP 791-18 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.63827, from Peterson et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023Natur.617..701P/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LP 791-18 (pscomppars): age 0.5 Gyr, from Peterson et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023Natur.617..701P/abstract)
